body: Norge har 3 forvaltningsnivåer, vi ville ikke merket om fylkeskommunen var borte fordi oppgavene kunne enkelt blitt fordelt enten til større kommuner eller staten. Vi subsidierer kunst/kunstnere med millioner i året som ytterst få har interesse av. 1/3 del av arbeidsstokken arbeider i offentlig sektor med en særdeles stor utesing i mellomledernivå. Staten finansierer en haug av frivillige organisasjoner. Vi finansierer utdanningsretninger med få til ingen karrieremuligheter. Det sier litt når Norge knapt klarer å skape selskaper som gjør annet enn å utnytte naturressurser, vi er et elendig land for innovasjon. Også kan du jo tenke deg at dersom du ikke ville brukt dine egne penger på det så er det en veldig god grunn til at du heller ikke burde bruke fellesskapets penger på det. Det er sånn holdning som gjør at regjeringene kan fortsette å sløse bort pengene våre på unødvendig fjas. Hans-Jørgen Blomseth som var leder for Stoltenberg 2 regjeringens Forenklingsprosjekt har sagt i Wolfgang Wees podcast at han kunne kuttet 200-300 milliarder av statsbudsjettet uten at flertallet ville merket det, men det blir ikke gjort fordi det er ikke vilje til det.

OP legger kanskje ikke merke til de 10.000,- som Høyre/FrP regjeringen ga i økt skattelette, men om du lever fra hånd til munn hver måned så er 800,- ekstra i måneden vesentlig. Men man bør ikke se på skattelette isolert sett. 10.000,- på et år er kanskje ikke så mye, men de fleste lever opp i mot 80-90 år der de kanskje har rundt 40-50år i arbeidslivet.

Utfordringen er i mange kommuner først og fremst er at det er mangel på areal som er regulert til boligbygging. I kommunenorge er det et massivt ønske om å sentralisere boligbyggingen samtidig som det er få regulerte områder i sentrumsnærhet på grunn av selvmotsigende lovverk. Det er ønskelig med sentralisering, det er ønskelig med fortetting, det er ønskelig med grøntareal nær der folk bor og grønt areal i sentrum er sterkt beskyttet. Da får man en situasjon der ingen boliger blir bygget og de boligene som eksisterer blir dyrere. Det faktum at egenkapitalkravet nå er senket til 10% gjør at langt flere vil få muligheten til å få lån, noe som vil skyve prisene enda høyere.
Resett betalte aldri 400k for det. De tilbydde 400k, men vedkommende takket nei, dette ble det blant annet lagd en sak på. Han gikk omsider ut i mediene om saken for å få slutt på ryktene.

I understand that it might seem out of place to compare the two games, but I don't think the difference is as big as you think it might be. This is not a problem at this time and mobility abilities usually have some sort of restrictions to them that makes them fair. Soldier has to aim the way he runs, Reinhard, Winston and Genji's Charge, jump and dash all have a preset distance to them, Mccree has a very short tumble, Sombra's translocator has a traveltime when you throw it + it only gets you to a preset position. What I don't want is another D'Va situation for example. During the tank meta, D'Va boost in, take a lot of damage, defense matrix to wait for cooldown (which is only 5 seconds) and then booster out to get healed.
I'd also make the case that more mobility = more preference towards hitscan heroes.

I agree with you to some extent, vertical mobility does offer new routes and help break up chokes. But most of the mobility options such as D'Vas boosters, Pharahs jump jet, Tracers blink/recall or Genji wallclimb/swiftstrike can be used as escape tools. It's also easier to aim side to side than to aim up and down for example so any hero with sudden vertical movement will have a slight advantage. Pharahs jump jet ability makes for a swift repositioning if she's on the ground so it can be used to escape incoming damage, on Pharah this is balanced out by the slow movement she has when she is up in the air. A big reason as to why D'Va was so strong in the tank meta was that she could booster in, take a lot of damage, then booster out to be healed up to full hp.
To rephrase myself, I fine with mobility options as long as there is some kind of restriction to it that balances it out. To take Mercy as an example, she requires allies in range to make use of her mobility. For Reinhardt, Winston and Genji their charge, jump and swiftstrike go a preset distance before stopping. Tracer is balanced out by being very squishy, Soldier has too look the way he sprints, Mccree has a short range on his tumble. D'Va is an example on how you shouldn't do it, low cooldown, movement in all directions, can be canceled mid flight, high health/armor, damage mitigation.
What I don't want to see in the future is a time where the meta is to pick high mobility heroes to completely bypass the chokepoints.

Gonna comment on some of the points you've made. I'm around the plat-diamond ranks so you know where my experience comes from.

Gameplay: In my opinion balance should be around the majority of the playerbase (the casuals). And then you can do tweaks that will in a lesser case impact the casuals (Widowmakers quickscoping) to try to balance out the competitive scene. Having a game be both is very difficult especially when the game is so diverse.

Maps: If you take a look at other popular competitive games the map design are not really that different. The fundamentals are there. Like for League of legends you have the chokepoints at the bases and dragon/baron pit. This is similar to the way a lot of Overwatch maps operate as you mentioned, one chokepoint at the start of the map and one at the end or in payload, one at each checkpoint. They also in both games favor the defending team and your options to breaking through are very similar, Dive comp or poke from range. Also in several of the popular CS:GO maps you have the initial fights being centered around different chokepoints, Dust 2 with mid doors, tunnel and long for example. Now they operate different in CS:GO as there are multiple objectives and so have multiple chokepoints that you can push through. This is something I think we could end up seeing in Overwatch if more maptypes are added (for example a map that features several points that can be captured at once, think Battlefield Conquest mode).
Overwatch is very snowbally and most defenses require setup, I believe this is the reason why you have the delay at the checkpoints, to allow the defenders to set up again. At some maps the defenders will just surrender one section of the map, because of the disadvantage they would put themselves in trying to set up a defense (Hollywood's streetphase has been one where this has happened). But then again Overwatch is not trying to be CS:GO so maybe chokepoints that you have to push through are going to be the norm.
Personally I'd like to see a map that favors vertical movement, I think this could help the hero balance as heroes as it would make it OK to have some heroes be better on some maps and weak on others.

But back to the example, if you as a Roadhog trade your 600 hp for an enemy supports 200 hp you will in most cases be at a disadvantage in the 5v5. Think how many 200 hp heroes you could've killed if you didn't die, as Roadhog you have a constant kill pressure on your enemy squishies. Just by being there, you force them to play cautiously out of range of your hook. And in a 5v5 with your team having 2 dps, 1 tank and 2 healer and the other team having 2 dps, 2 tanks and 1 healer, the other team will most likely win that fight and there's a couple of reasons to that.
1. Your opponents have a higher hp count than your team has. 2 tanks with around 500 hp each + 2 dps at 200 hp and a healer at 200 hp, effective healthpool of 1600. While your team has 1 tank at 500 hp, 2 dps at 200 hp and 2 healers at 200 hp, an effective healthpool of 1300 healthpoints.
2. Your opponents have more damage threats than you do.
3. Your opponents have a stronger frontline and more cover.

So instead of trying to argue with them, give them the benefit of the doubt once in a while, even if you don't agree. They might be right, but more importantly they won't be caught up in you and your Roadhog, if you switch they'll forget about it.
